description: Make proposal-candidate retirement actually retire: move the row to 'archived' so selection stops re-promoting it and its research problem is released. Bill undelivered proposal spend to the research problem rather than the candidate row, so releasing a problem does not hand it a fresh budget share, and decline to seed a problem already over that ceiling.
preconditions: Explicit grouped production-write and service-restart authorization is recorded for this batch.
R8 snapshot shows zero active Deepgraph experiment runs, attempt reservations, queued/running GPU jobs, and Colab requests.
A PostgreSQL custom-format backup and the OPERATORS.log predeployment snapshot are recorded before services stop.
Live targets match the previously deployed commit 8316ddd (v1-duplicate-calibration); a mismatch means another session wrote the tree and the deploy stops.
Unrelated GPU workloads on the two A100 hosts are not stopped or modified.
deployment_steps: Stop deepgraph-auto-advance.timer AND deepgraph-auto-advance.service, deepgraph-auto-execute.service, deepgraph-observe@10, deepgraph-observe@11, and deepgraph-web.service only after R8 is zero. Stopping the timer alone leaves the running pass in place; the observers are included because their idle-in-transaction AccessShareLock blocked an earlier batch.
Apply batch 1 through scripts/deploy_manifest_batch.py and verify every deployed SHA256.
py_compile the three runtime modules in the live tree.
Restart web, observers, auto-execute, then the auto-advance timer.
Append every production action, backup path, checksum, restart, and health result to OPERATORS.log.
After restart, make no manual business-state calls; observe only normal services/timer.
tests: Full suite 72 failed / 807 passed / 18 skipped / 3 collection errors, identical failure and collection-error count to baseline; all six meta-harness audits pass (static/scope/sql passed, llm_caller unclassified=0, state_authority authority_violations=0, backend reports no violations). The eleven new tests fail against the pre-change source and pass after it.

rollback.order: stop services after R8 zero, then reverse batch 1
steps: Use deploy_manifest_batch.py --rollback for 1-retire-and-bill-problem; each restored file must match its recorded predeployment SHA256.
No schema change, no .env change, and no systemd unit change is part of this batch, so nothing else needs reversing.
Restart deepgraph-web.service, the observers, and deepgraph-auto-execute.service, then enable/start deepgraph-auto-advance.timer.
Record rollback commands, restored hashes, service states, and health results in OPERATORS.log.
rollback.data_impact: Additive only; no schema change. The batch writes deep_insights.status='archived' for candidates that exhausted their problem's proposal budget share. 'archived' is an existing status the pre-change code already excludes from candidate selection (agents/paper_idea_agent.py, agents/agenda_repository.py, scripts/auto_advance.py), so rolling back leaves archived candidates archived and their problems released, rather than resurrecting the per-pass promote/refuse/retire churn. Rolling back does restore the per-idea ceiling, so a problem released before rollback could then be funded again from zero; the ceiling still bounds it to one further share.

batches.purpose: Deploy the terminal retirement status, the problem-scoped undelivered-proposal ceiling, and the seeding guard at R8 zero.
batches.health_check: Re-hash every deployed target, py_compile the three modules, confirm GET / returns 200 on 8080 with no /home/ paths in /api/stats.
batches.acceptance: Every deployed SHA256 equals this manifest; no live attempt or GPU job crosses the deployment boundary.
